findings.title: Sponsored invoke is not bound to its declared contract and accepts contract-credential auth without checks
Sponsored row stored without binding the invoked contract, function or auth entries to SponsoredAccount
Env distribution signer signs any envelope it is given without checking its operations
Signer router signs whatever transaction it is given, including sponsored XDR that makes the distribution account the operation source
Payment source wallet is not bound to the transaction's tenant
BulkInsert stores a wallet_id without checking the tenant owns that distribution wallet
Wallet-creation handler signs RPC-supplied auth entries without validating them, unlike the sponsored handler
Reprocessing erases the submitted hash and envelope, so a landed payment is rebuilt and paid again
Lowercase 'xlm' asset code passes validation but is built as a credit asset and stalls the payment job
Wallet-creation fee is the classic max base fee and omits the Soroban resource fee
No fail-closed per-payment amount cap before the distribution account signs
Reconciliation identifies a submission by the fee-bump outer hash, so a payment that landed under another wrapper is paid again
Every payment is submitted with the SEP-29 memo-required check disabled
Channel-account creation deletes signing keys after a submit that may have landed
Sponsored Soroban invocations are built with the classic base fee and no resource fee, so they are rejected as insufficient fee
CreateAndFundAccount accepts an unbounded, possibly negative native amount from the host account
CreateAndFundAccount signs with the host key while the transaction source is sourceAcc
StoreKey stores a secret without checking it matches the public key or is a valid seed
Channel-account rollback delete fails when the ledger has advanced, leaving unfunded channel-account rows
Batch deletion treats an empty result as an error, so the clean-exit branch is dead and a partial delete returns failure
Simulation error response is ignored, so an empty transaction is built and submitted
Decrypted distribution secret is not checked against the requested public key before signing
Wallet key row is written without binding its public key to the ciphertext it protects
Terminal status writes are not conditioned on PROCESSING in the database
Wallet-creation row stored without the required public key and wasm hash length
Deterministic preparation errors are never terminal: the job stays locked, is reselected and retried forever while reporting to the crash tracker
Any Horizon error not on the terminal list is retried indefinitely, including permanent rejections such as op_malformed or tx_malformed
CreateAndFundAccount retries after non-Horizon errors and treats op_already_exists as retriable, so a landed funding is reported as failed
Simulation error field is ignored; the handler builds and submits a transaction with no Soroban data after the RPC reports a failure
VerifyChannelAccounts deletes DB rows without checking the lock, so in-use channel accounts can be removed

findings.title: Dispatch failure leaves locked bundles stuck and reselected every cycle
Adaptive back-off raises the bundle limit instead of lowering it
AddTrustlines sets an empty trustline limit, which means the maximum limit
DeleteKey enforces none of the documented guard for active or funded wallets
Wallet key row can be deleted with no tenant, state or balance check
